hook: In 1963, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler captured the ruins of Coventry on her vintage film camera.

sections.voiceover: In 1963, 17-year-old Elizabeth Tyler captured the ruins of Coventry on her vintage film camera.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a vintage black and white photograph showing a bomb site in Coventry.

sections.voiceover: Elizabeth Tyler wandered through the city's abandoned bomb sites to record the decay. Did this Coventry College of Art student know her 1933 Rolleicord camera would document history?
sections.visual_cue: Historical still of a young woman holding a Rolleicord camera, followed by shots of rubble-strewn streets.

sections.voiceover: Tyler's archive of Coventry bomb sites remained hidden for six decades before their recent rediscovery.
sections.visual_cue: Archive footage of a dusty, closed-up cardboard box being opened.

sections.voiceover: This archive immortalizes the city as it stood in 1963 through her unique photographic lens.
sections.visual_cue: Panning shot over the pages of a slim, staple-bound book featuring stark, monochromatic photography.

sections.voiceover: Her 1933 camera turned a forgotten city into a lasting archive.
sections.visual_cue: Final shot of the Rolleicord camera resting on a table beside the printed book.
